purpose: Harden callisto-graph's core identity-promotion mechanism in crates/callisto-graph/src/identity.rs and crates/callisto-graph/src/walk.rs so that: (1) IdentityIndex.prefixed is populated during ManifestWalkResolver::build for every discovered (ecosystem, native-name) pair, so ecosystem-prefixed group-member spellings such as cargo:foo resolve; (2) two or more genuinely distinct packages sharing a bare name across different ecosystems, at different paths, are promoted to PackageId::Prefixed and recognized as distinct packages instead of colliding into GraphError::DuplicatePackage, for N=2 and N>2 collisions and independent of by-path iteration order; (3) IdentityIndex::resolve_native_with_fallback never silently satisfies a same-ecosystem dependency-name miss with a cross-ecosystem name match during edge extraction; and (4) resolve_package_config's ambiguity detection correctly reports GraphError::AmbiguousName when an unprefixed [[package]] rule matches two or more promoted siblings, with a promotion-data-sourcing mechanism that is correct for each of resolve_package_config's two real call sites given their genuinely different execution timing relative to ManifestWalkResolver::build.
scope:
crates/callisto-graph/src/identity.rs (IdentityIndex.prefixed population contract; IdentityIndex::resolve_native, unchanged; IdentityIndex::resolve_native_with_fallback, corrected no-cross-ecosystem-fallback-on-miss behavior) and crates/callisto-graph/src/walk.rs (ManifestWalkResolver::build's by-path collision loop at walk.rs:72-134: package_manifest_decls construction, index.bare/index.native/index.platform population, and the promotion-vs-DuplicatePackage decision; and the edge-extraction call site at walk.rs:360-364 that calls resolve_native_with_fallback). api_surface.name: Data structures and their lifecycle
api_surface.signature: N/A -- this entry is a reference table read before any other api_surface entry or acceptance criterion; every other entry cross-references it instead of re-explaining timing inline.
api_surface.description:
Every piece of state this mechanism introduces or reads, in the order it becomes relevant during a single Workspace::load call. All line numbers verified by direct read of the current source this session.

1. `package_manifest_decls: BTreeMap<PackageId, (PathBuf, Vec<ManifestDecl>)>` -- LOCAL to ManifestWalkResolver::build, declared at walk.rs:53-54. Populated during the by-path collision loop (walk.rs:72-134), one entry per distinct primary_id. INVARIANT once the loop completes: exactly one entry per promoted-or-unpromoted package identity that survived without triggering DuplicatePackage; never holds two entries for the same PackageId. ROUND-2 CORRECTION: the current source's collision-insert pattern at walk.rs:126-128 reads `if let Some((existing_path, _)) = package_manifest_decls.insert(primary_id.clone(), (rel_path.clone(), decls)) { ... }` -- the underscore discards the first-seen path's own `Vec<ManifestDecl>` the instant a collision is detected, before promotion is decided. This spec's stale-key rewrite step (location (4) in the ManifestWalkResolver::build entry's STALE-KEY REWRITE list below) needs that discarded value to correctly rewrite the first-seen path's package_manifest_decls entry once promotion fires -- an implementation that leaves the pattern as `(existing_path, _)` has no way to recover it. This spec requires changing the pattern to bind the decls: `if let Some((existing_path, existing_decls)) = package_manifest_decls.insert(...)`. `existing_decls` (the first-seen path's own manifests, now retained rather than discarded) feeds the first-seen path's promoted package_manifest_decls entry; the current path's own already-in-scope `decls` local variable (populated earlier in the same per-path loop iteration, walk.rs:84-124) feeds the current path's promoted entry. Neither path's decls are ever mixed into the other's entry.

2. `index: IdentityIndex` (fields `bare`, `prefixed`, `native`, `platform`) -- LOCAL to build, declared at walk.rs:55 as `IdentityIndex::default()`, populated during the same by-path collision loop (walk.rs:72-134), and returned as part of `ManifestWalkResolver` at build's end (walk.rs:389-396, field `index`). Fully populated and immutable from that point on for the rest of the `Workspace`'s lifetime. INVARIANTS once build() returns: `index.native` contains one entry per (ecosystem, native-name) pair actually discovered, each value the post-promotion PackageId (Prefixed if promoted, Bare otherwise) -- never a stale pre-promotion id. `index.bare` contains no key whose name has ever been promoted (see AC-06). `index.prefixed` contains one entry per (ecosystem, native-name) pair discovered WHOSE MANIFEST'S OWN DECLARED NAME EQUALS ITS PATH'S PRIMARY IDENTITY'S NAME (ROUND-7 CORRECTION: not every discovered pair unconditionally -- see the IdentityIndex.prefixed api_surface entry for why an unrestricted population regresses AC-13/napi drift detection), for every such package regardless of whether it was promoted (see AC-02), each such entry's value the post-promotion PackageId (Prefixed if promoted, Bare otherwise) -- ROUND-9 ADDITION: never a stale pre-promotion id, exactly the same never-stale invariant already stated for index.native and index.platform below; see the ManifestWalkResolver::build entry's STALE-KEY REWRITE location (5) for the exact rewrite procedure this requires -- this is a superset of the promoted subset, but NOT a superset of every entry index.native holds: a differently-named manifest sharing a path with its primary identity (an npm platform manifest) contributes an index.native entry but never an index.prefixed entry. `index.platform` contains one entry per discovered npm Platform-role manifest, keyed by that manifest's own declared name, valued with its current owning PackageId (Prefixed if the owner was promoted, Bare otherwise) -- never a stale pre-promotion owner id.

3. `claiming_ecosystems: BTreeMap<PathBuf, BTreeSet<Ecosystem>>` -- LOCAL to ManifestWalkResolver::build, declared alongside `package_manifest_decls`/`index`/`diagnostics` (walk.rs:53-56). ROUND-4 ADDITION, closing a gap in the round-2/round-3 design: the PROMOTION PREDICATE (in the ManifestWalkResolver::build entry, below) needs, for the FIRST-SEEN path in a pairwise collision, that path's own name-scoped claiming-ecosystem set -- but by the moment a collision is detected (the second path's `package_manifest_decls.insert` returns `Some`), the first-seen path's own per-path loop iteration has already fully completed, and nothing retained about it (`existing_decls`, item 1's `Vec<ManifestDecl>`) carries a `name` field to recompute that set from (`ManifestDecl` has only `path`/`role`/`format`, confirmed against crates/callisto-model/src/package.rs:82-86 -- no `name` field exists). `package_ecosystems` (walk.rs:165's `decls.iter().map(|d| d.ecosystem())`, used later for `[[package-set]]`/`[[package]]` matching) is also not a substitute: it is a path's FULL ecosystem membership, including e.g. an npm Platform manifest whose own declared name differs from the path's primary bare name, which over-counts relative to the name-scoped set the predicate needs (an npm Platform entry at the same path as a Cargo canonical manifest must NOT count toward the claiming-ecosystem set for the Cargo manifest's bare name, or AC-13's fixture wrongly collides as same-ecosystem). FIX: populate `claiming_ecosystems` for EVERY path (not only ones that turn out to collide), at the top of each by-path loop iteration (walk.rs:72 onward) immediately after `primary_id` is computed (walk.rs:78, right after the `list.sort_by_key` call): filter that path's own `list: Vec<(Ecosystem, PackageId)>` local (populated per-path at walk.rs:64-70, one entry per manifest actually discovered at that path, each carrying that manifest's OWN declared identity) down to entries whose `id.name()` equals `primary_id.name()`, and collect the DISTINCT ecosystems of just those name-matching entries into a `BTreeSet<Ecosystem>`; insert `(rel_path.clone(), that_set)` into `claiming_ecosystems`. INVARIANT: exactly one entry per path visited by the by-path loop, every stored set non-empty (every path has at least one manifest whose declared name equals that path's own primary bare name, since `primary_id` is itself drawn from `list`). USAGE: the PROMOTION PREDICATE's branch (i) (the first pairwise collision) reads BOTH colliding paths' sets from this map -- `claiming_ecosystems.get(&existing_path)` for the first-seen path (recoverable here for the first time; `existing_decls` alone cannot supply it) and `claiming_ecosystems.get(&rel_path)` for the current path -- to run the disjointness test. Once promotion is decided, each promoted path's own set (already held in this map) is copied alongside its newly-promoted `PackageId` into `promoted_siblings` (item 4 below), which is the map ALREADY-PROMOTED-NAME DETECTION's branch (ii) reads for every EXISTING group member's retained set -- branch (ii) does not re-query `claiming_ecosystems` for existing members, it reads their sets from `promoted_siblings`' own stored tuples (item 4's design); branch (ii) reads `claiming_ecosystems` only for the newly-arriving third-or-later path's own set, computed and stored the same way as every other path. This local map is never read, written, or referenced outside `ManifestWalkResolver::build`, and its values are never conflated with `package_ecosystems` (over-counts) and never re-derived from `decls`/`existing_decls` (lack names).

ROUND-7 ADDITION, closing a further gap `claiming_ecosystems` alone cannot close: `claiming_ecosystems` is deliberately NAME-SCOPED (filtered to entries whose declared name equals the path's own primary bare name), which is exactly what the PROMOTION PREDICATE and ALREADY-PROMOTED-NAME DETECTION need -- but it is NOT sufficient input for the STALE-KEY REWRITE step (location (3) in the ManifestWalkResolver::build entry, below), because index.native itself is NOT name-scoped (per the IdentityIndex.prefixed api_surface entry's Round-7 correction, index.native keeps its full, unrestricted population -- one entry per (ecosystem, id) pair in a path's own `list`, using each manifest's own declared name as the key, even when that name differs from the path's primary_id.name(), e.g. an npm Platform manifest). When a path is promoted, EVERY index.native entry that path ever inserted must be rewritten to the new Prefixed id (STALE-KEY REWRITE location (3)) -- including a Platform manifest's differently-named entry, which `claiming_ecosystems` does not track (by design, since it is excluded from the name-scoped set). For the CURRENT path in a per-path loop iteration this is not a problem: that path's own `list` local is still in scope and can be read directly. It IS a problem for the FIRST-SEEN path in branch (i)'s pairwise collision (see the GUARD and STALE-KEY REWRITE sections below): by the time the collision is detected, that path's own loop iteration, and its `list` local, are gone, and neither `existing_decls` (no name field) nor `claiming_ecosystems.get(&existing_path)` (name-scoped only, would omit the Platform entry) can recover it. FIX: alongside `claiming_ecosystems`, populate a second retained local map at the same point in the same per-path loop preamble (immediately after `primary_id` is computed, walk.rs:78): `path_native_keys: BTreeMap<PathBuf, Vec<(Ecosystem, String)>>`, storing, for every path visited (collision or not), the COMPLETE, UNFILTERED list of (ecosystem, id.name().to_string()) pairs from that path's own `list` -- exactly the set of keys that path will insert into index.native, with no name-match restriction. `path_native_keys.get(&existing_path)` is what the STALE-KEY REWRITE's location (3) reads to correctly rewrite the first-seen path's full set of index.native entries at promotion time, including any Platform-manifest entry whose name never entered the PROMOTION PREDICATE's disjointness check. This map is never read, written, or referenced outside `ManifestWalkResolver::build`, is distinct in purpose from `claiming_ecosystems` (which remains the sole input to the PROMOTION PREDICATE and ALREADY-PROMOTED-NAME DETECTION, unchanged), and is never used as a substitute for it.

4. `promoted_siblings: BTreeMap<String, Vec<(PackageId, BTreeSet<Ecosystem>)>>` (LOCAL, build-scoped) -- a new local variable declared inside ManifestWalkResolver::build alongside `package_manifest_decls`/`index`/`diagnostics` (walk.rs:53-56), NOT a field on any struct. ROUND-2 RETYPE (was `BTreeMap<String, Vec<PackageId>>`): a bare `Vec<PackageId>` cannot represent a Case D member's full ecosystem footprint once that member is inside a promoted group, because `PackageId::Prefixed` itself encodes only ONE ecosystem (its own primary_ecosystem field) -- storing only the PackageId loses the very set the ALREADY-PROMOTED-NAME DETECTION disjointness check (below) needs to re-check against every existing group member. Each Vec entry is therefore a pair: the promoted member's PackageId, together with that SAME path's full name-scoped claiming-ecosystem set (the identical set the PROMOTION PREDICATE, below, already reads per-path from `claiming_ecosystems` (item 3) to decide promotion -- retained here, alongside the newly-promoted PackageId, rather than left only in `claiming_ecosystems` once the decision is made). Accumulated during the same by-path collision loop (walk.rs:72-134): each time the PROMOTION PREDICATE decides promotion rather than DuplicatePackage, both colliding paths' (newly-promoted PackageId::Prefixed, that path's own claiming-ecosystem set) pairs are pushed onto `promoted_siblings.entry(name.clone()).or_default()`. Fully populated once the loop (walk.rs:72-134) completes, still entirely inside the same build() call, well before build() returns. INVARIANT: every value Vec has length >= 2, every key is a bare name that collided across a disjoint ecosystem set at least once during this build() call, and every stored ecosystem set is non-empty. This local map is the sole input to `cfg.with_promoted_siblings(...)` (item 6 below) and is never read, written, or referenced outside ManifestWalkResolver::build.

5. `ResolvedConfig.promoted_siblings: pub(crate) BTreeMap<String, Vec<(PackageId, BTreeSet<Ecosystem>)>>` (a FIELD on ResolvedConfig, config/resolve.rs) -- distinct from item 4 above despite the identical logical shape; matched to a different call site's timing. ROUND-2 RETYPE: same pair-shape change as item 4, for the same reason (a Case D member's full claiming-ecosystem set must survive independently of its single-ecosystem PackageId). Default-constructed as `BTreeMap::new()` wherever `config::load` builds its `Ok(ResolvedConfig { .. })` literal (config/resolve.rs, confirmed the struct's fields at resolve.rs:15-42; the construction site is later in the same file), since promotion is unknown at config-load time -- identity has not yet been discovered. Populated in `Workspace::load` (lib.rs), on the line immediately after `config.groups = GroupTable::resolve(&config.raw_groups, graph.identity())?;` (lib.rs:109): iterate `graph.identity().prefixed` (item 2 above, confirmed populated by that point since `graph` is `ManifestWalkResolver::build`'s own return value from lib.rs:107, which has already returned), group each `(Ecosystem, String) -> PackageId` entry by its name; for each distinct name, collect the distinct PackageIds sharing it, and for EACH distinct PackageId, collect every ecosystem whose `(Ecosystem, name)` entry maps to that same PackageId into that PackageId's own `BTreeSet<Ecosystem>` (this is how a Case D member's full multi-ecosystem set is reconstructed from `prefixed`'s single-ecosystem-keyed entries -- the same PackageId recurs once per ecosystem it claims the name in). Retain only names whose distinct-id count is 2 or more. A genuine Case D package's two-or-more per-ecosystem `prefixed` entries are excluded because they all share the SAME single `PackageId` -- one shared identity, since it genuinely is one package spanning multiple ecosystems (see item 2's INVARIANT and AC-11) -- so grouping by name yields a distinct-id count of exactly 1 for that name, failing the 2-or-more retention test, REGARDLESS of whether that one shared id happens to be `Bare` (an unpromoted Case D package, AC-11) or `Prefixed` (a Case D package whose bare name also collided with a third, disjoint-ecosystem path and was itself promoted -- e.g. AC-21's aaa/tri). `prefixed` is NOT promoted-only -- per item 2 and AC-02, it holds one entry per (ecosystem, native-name) pair for EVERY discovered package, promoted or not -- so the correct exclusion reason is the shared-id count, never the value's Bare-vs-Prefixed variant. A promoted pair's two-or-more `prefixed` entries, by contrast, carry two or more genuinely DISTINCT `PackageId`s (one per promoted sibling), so grouping by name yields a distinct-id count of 2 or more and the name is retained, each distinct id paired with its own reconstructed ecosystem set. SCOPE OF THIS FIELD, PRECISELY: reachable and correctly populated only from `Workspace::load`, strictly AFTER `ManifestWalkResolver::build` has already returned (lib.rs:107 calls build; lib.rs:109-110 run only once `graph` exists). This field is the correct and sufficient data source for aggregate.rs:211's call site (item 7b below) -- that call site runs later still, inside a separate command invocation (via commands/version.rs:39), well after Workspace::load has finished. This field is NOT a valid data source for walk.rs:175's call site (item 7a below): that call site executes DURING ManifestWalkResolver::build, before `graph` (build's own eventual return value) exists, so this field is unconditionally still its `BTreeMap::new()` default at that point in execution -- an implementation that reads `cfg.promoted_siblings` (this field) at walk.rs:175 can never observe a populated map and the AmbiguousName branch could never fire there.

6. `ResolvedConfig::with_promoted_siblings(&self, promoted_siblings: BTreeMap<String, Vec<(PackageId, BTreeSet<Ecosystem>)>>) -> ResolvedConfig` -- a new crate-internal method defined inside config/resolve.rs (the only module with access to ResolvedConfig's private `provenance` field, so a full `self.clone()` plus single-field overwrite is required rather than a cross-module struct-update literal). Parameter type retyped in round 2 to match items 4/5. Called exactly once per ManifestWalkResolver::build invocation, after the by-path collision loop (walk.rs:72-134) has finished populating item 4 (the local `promoted_siblings` map) and before the second, per-package loop that contains walk.rs:175 begins (that loop starts at walk.rs:144, immediately after the `let mut packages = BTreeMap::new();` setup line at walk.rs:143). Produces a single, build-local `ResolvedConfig` overlay value carrying build's own local promotion map (item 4), leaving the original `cfg: &ResolvedConfig` parameter build() received untouched. This overlay value exists only for the duration of build()'s remaining execution; it is never returned, stored, or referenced after build() returns.

7. `resolve_package_config`'s two call sites, each reading a different one of the above:
   (a) walk.rs:175, inside ManifestWalkResolver::build's second per-package loop (walk.rs:144 onward): reads a reference to the build-local overlay from item 6 (`&cfg_with_local_promotions`), NOT build's own `cfg` parameter and NOT item 5. Executes once per package, entirely within a single build() call, after item 4 is fully populated and item 6's overlay has been constructed.
   (b) aggregate.rs:211, inside `aggregate()`: reads `config`, the `&ResolvedConfig` `aggregate()` itself received as a parameter, unmodified -- by the time `aggregate()` runs (called from commands/version.rs:39, always after a `Workspace::load` call has fully completed for that same config), item 5 is already correctly populated by lib.rs:109-110. `with_promoted_siblings` (item 6) is never called on this path.
   Both call sites invoke the exact same function signature, `resolve_package_config(id: &PackageId, cfg: &ResolvedConfig) -> Result<Option<&PackageConfig>, GraphError>` -- only which `ResolvedConfig` reference each site passes as the second argument differs, and that difference is confined to walk.rs:175's local overlay construction; nothing about `resolve_package_config`'s or `aggregate()`'s own signature changes.

api_surface.name: IdentityIndex.prefixed
api_surface.description:
Must be populated during ManifestWalkResolver::build's by-path collision loop (walk.rs:72-134) -- but, ROUND-7 CORRECTION, NOT by blindly mirroring every entry index.native receives, and NOT for every (ecosystem, native-name) pair discovered. index.native (walk.rs:121-123) is populated once per (ecosystem, id) pair in a path's own `list`, keyed by that manifest's OWN declared name, regardless of whether that name matches the path's primary_id.name() -- this unrestricted population is required, pre-existing, unrelated behavior this spec's non_goals do not permit changing (it is what lets the real disk-discovered `optional_dependency_on_case_d_platform_package_resolves_via_native_index` test in walk.rs resolve a dependency naming an npm platform manifest by that manifest's own, differently-spelled name). index.prefixed must NOT copy that unrestricted population. Only insert a (eco, id.name()) -> primary_id entry into index.prefixed when id.name() == primary_id.name() for that path -- i.e. when the manifest being indexed actually declares, as its own name, the same name that is that path's primary bare identity (the ordinary single-manifest case, and the genuine Case D case where every ecosystem's manifest at a path shares one identical name). A manifest whose own declared name differs from its path's primary_id.name() -- the defining trait of an npm platform manifest, e.g. "@myorg/native-core-linux-x64-gnu" at a path whose primary_id is "native-core" -- must NOT gain a prefixed entry under its own distinct name.

WHY THIS RESTRICTION IS REQUIRED (traced against real source this session): IdentityIndex::resolve_human's existing candidates loop (identity.rs:267-272, unchanged by this spec) matches the raw lookup string directly against each prefixed entry's native-name component (`if n == name`) -- no colon-prefix parsing is needed for this match to fire. If prefixed were populated unrestricted (mirroring native), a `[[fixed-group]] members` entry naming a platform manifest by its own bare, unprefixed name (e.g. "@myorg/native-core-linux-x64-gnu", the exact form AC-13's fixture uses) would find exactly one candidate via this existing loop -- the platform manifest's own prefixed entry -- and resolve_human would return Ok(primary_id) via the candidates.len() == 1 branch (identity.rs:274-276) BEFORE GroupTable::resolve ever reaches its own index.platform.get(name) fallback. Confirmed this session against config/groups.rs: GroupTable::resolve tries `index.resolve_human(name, &[])` FIRST (groups.rs:147 for fixed groups, :178 for linked groups) and only falls through to `index.platform.get(name)` in an `else if` (groups.rs:150, :181) when resolve_human errors. An unrestricted prefixed population would make resolve_human succeed for a platform manifest's own name, so GroupTable::resolve would push a `GroupMember::Package` instead of the correct `GroupMember::PlatformManifest` -- silently breaking napi.rs's drift-check filtering, which (confirmed this session, napi.rs:77-83, `napi_drift`'s `group.members(GroupMemberKind::PlatformManifest)` call) only ever inspects `GroupMember::PlatformManifest` entries and would never see this member at all. This is precisely the regression this spec's own AC-13 asserts must not happen. The restriction stated above (index.prefixed only gains an entry when id.name() == primary_id.name()) prevents it: a platform manifest's own differently-named entry is excluded from prefixed by construction, so resolve_human's candidates loop finds nothing for it, correctly falls through to Err(UnknownPackage), and GroupTable::resolve correctly reaches its index.platform.get(name) fallback.

This restriction does not affect AC-01/AC-02 (an ordinary single-ecosystem Cargo package's own declared name trivially equals its own primary_id.name(), since primary_id is drawn directly from that manifest's own identity) or AC-08's underlying Case D member (every ecosystem's manifest at that path declares the identical shared bare name, so id.name() == primary_id.name() holds for every one of that path's ecosystems, and every one of them gains a prefixed entry).

Currently this field is declared on IdentityIndex (identity.rs:238) and is never written anywhere in walk.rs -- this is bug #1 this spec fixes.

ROUND-4 CORRECTION (this field's population alone does NOT make AC-01 resolvable -- resolve_human itself must also change): the existing resolve_human loop over self.prefixed (identity.rs:267-272: `for ((_eco, n), id) in &self.prefixed { if n == name { candidates.push(id.clone()); } }`) compares the map's native-name component (`n`, e.g. "foo") against the RAW, still-prefixed lookup string (`name`, e.g. "cargo:foo") -- these can never match, since one is a bare name and the other still carries its colon-prefix. Populating self.prefixed does not by itself make AC-01's scenario reachable through that loop; it falls through to UnknownPackage exactly as before. IdentityIndex::resolve_human (identity.rs:252-298) must gain a new lookup branch, inserted as the FIRST check performed -- before the existing `self.bare.get(name)` lookup at identity.rs:263: call `PackageId::parse(name)` (callisto-model/src/identity.rs:24-81); if it succeeds and yields `PackageId::Prefixed { ecosystem, name: n }` (i.e. the input string carried a recognized ecosystem prefix, e.g. "cargo:foo" -> Prefixed{Cargo, "foo"}), look up `self.prefixed.get(&(ecosystem, n))` directly and, if found, return `Ok(stored.clone())` immediately -- `stored` is this field's own value for that pair, which per AC-02 is always the package's real, current primary identity (Bare for an unpromoted package, Prefixed for a promoted one), never a synthesized id and never a value absent from the packages map. This new branch replaces the current first block (identity.rs:257-261: `if let Ok(id) = PackageId::parse(name) { if self.bare.values().any(|v| v == &id) || self.prefixed.values().any(|v| v == &id) { return Ok(id); } }`), which is dead-in-practice for the Prefixed case (a package's stored self.prefixed value equals the freshly-parsed `id` only when that package happens to already be stored as that exact synthesized Prefixed value, which excludes every unpromoted package, including AC-01's) and redundant for the Bare case (the very next block, `self.bare.get(name)`, already handles unprefixed lookups directly). Do NOT instead change what value gets stored in self.prefixed (e.g. storing a synthesized Prefixed id in place of the real primary_id) to make the old id-membership check pass instead -- that would break AC-02 (which requires prefixed's value to equal native's value for the same pair) and would make resolve_human return an identity that is not a real key in the packages map. Verified effects: AC-01 becomes genuinely reachable (self.prefixed.get(&(Cargo,"foo")) finds the unpromoted package's own Bare("foo") id and returns it via the new branch). AC-03 is unaffected and still correctly fails with MissingGroupMember: self.prefixed.get(&(Npm,"foo")) is None (no npm foo exists in that fixture), so the new branch's inner `if let Some(id) = ...` is not taken and execution falls through unchanged to the existing bare-name/candidates logic, returning Err(UnknownPackage) (mapped to MissingGroupMember by the group-resolution caller). AC-06 is unaffected: an unprefixed lookup string ("native-core", no colon) parses to PackageId::Bare, never PackageId::Prefixed, so the new branch's `if let Ok(PackageId::Prefixed{..})` guard never matches for it, and execution proceeds to the existing bare-map-then-candidates logic exactly as before. This field is also, per the Data-structures-and-lifecycle entry's item 5 (renumbered from item 4 in this round -- see the new item 3, claiming_ecosystems, inserted ahead of it), the sole data source Workspace::load reads to derive ResolvedConfig.promoted_siblings -- no separate promotion-bookkeeping collection is threaded out of ManifestWalkResolver for that purpose.

api_surface.name: ManifestWalkResolver::build (package identity collision keying)
api_surface.signature: pub fn build<L: ProjectLocator, R: CommandRunner>(root: &Path, locator: &L, _runner: &R, cfg: &ResolvedConfig, manifest_cache: &RefCell<BTreeMap<PathBuf, Arc<dyn Manifest>>>) -> Result<Self, GraphError>
api_surface.description:
The by-path grouping (walk.rs:64-70) and per-path primary_id selection via ecosystem_primary_priority (walk.rs:73-78, Case D collapse) are already correct and unchanged. The package_manifest_decls.insert collision point (walk.rs:126-128, error at walk.rs:129-133) must, before erroring, distinguish 'same bare name claimed at two different paths in two different ecosystems' (promote both occurrences' PackageId to PackageId::Prefixed{ecosystem, name}, no error) from 'same bare name claimed at two different paths in the same ecosystem' (GraphError::DuplicatePackage{id, paths}, unchanged) and from 'same path, multiple ecosystems' (already collapsed upstream via ecosystem_primary_priority sorting, walk.rs:77-78, and never reaches this collision point). ROUND-2 CORRECTION TO THE INSERT SITE ITSELF: change the discard pattern `if let Some((existing_path, _)) = package_manifest_decls.insert(...)` to `if let Some((existing_path, existing_decls)) = package_manifest_decls.insert(...)` -- see the Data-structures-and-lifecycle entry's item 1 for exactly which decls source (`existing_decls` vs. the current path's own already-in-scope `decls`) feeds which promoted entry's rewrite in STALE-KEY REWRITE location (4) below.

PROMOTION PREDICATE: capture each colliding path's NAME-SCOPED CLAIMING-ECOSYSTEM SET for the specific colliding bare name -- the set of ecosystems in which that path's OWN manifests declare a native name (the id.name() value used as the index.native key at walk.rs:121-123) equal to the colliding bare name being disambiguated -- NOT the path's full ecosystem set (`package_ecosystems`, the `decls.iter().map(|d| d.ecosystem())` derivation at walk.rs:165, which counts every ecosystem the path has any manifest in regardless of declared name). ROUND-4 CORRECTION: this set is READ, never re-derived, from the `claiming_ecosystems: BTreeMap<PathBuf, BTreeSet<Ecosystem>>` local map (Data-structures-and-lifecycle item 3), which is populated for every path -- collision or not -- at the top of that path's own loop iteration, before this predicate ever runs for it. This matters specifically at the moment `package_manifest_decls.insert` first returns `Some` (branch (i), the first pairwise collision): by that point the FIRST-SEEN colliding path's own loop iteration has already fully completed, and `existing_decls` (the value bound at the collision-insert site, item 1) carries no `name` field to recompute its claiming-ecosystem set from (`ManifestDecl` has only `path`/`role`/`format`) -- `claiming_ecosystems.get(&existing_path)` is the ONLY way to recover the first-seen path's set at this point, and `claiming_ecosystems.get(&rel_path)` supplies the current, colliding path's own set. These genuinely differ from `package_ecosystems`: an npm Platform-role manifest (walk.rs:101-108) at the same path as a Cargo canonical manifest contributes Npm to that path's package_ecosystems even when its own declared name (e.g. "@myorg/native-core-linux-x64-gnu") differs from the Cargo manifest's name (e.g. "native-core") -- that Platform entry must NOT count toward the claiming-ecosystem set for the bare name "native-core", or AC-21's fixture would wrongly collide as same-ecosystem; `claiming_ecosystems`' own name-filtered population rule (item 3) excludes it by construction. For an ordinary single-ecosystem path this set has one member; for a genuine Case D path whose two-or-more manifests all declare the SAME bare name this set has two or more members (e.g. {Cargo, Npm}). Promote (do not error) only when the two paths' name-scoped claiming-ecosystem sets, both read from `claiming_ecosystems`, are FULLY DISJOINT -- no ecosystem appears in both. When the sets share even one ecosystem, GraphError::DuplicatePackage{id, paths}, never promote -- this is a set-DISJOINTNESS test, not a set-inequality test: {Cargo, Npm} and {Npm} are unequal but NOT disjoint (share Npm), so they error (AC-08 depends on this); {Cargo, Npm} and {Pypi} are disjoint, so they promote. This predicate subsumes the two-single-ecosystem case (AC-04/AC-05/AC-06/AC-07) and additionally resolves the Case-D-vs-third-path case (AC-08).

This PREDICATE (which ecosystems trigger promotion vs. DuplicatePackage) is distinct from the REWRITE below (which stale-key locations get updated once promotion is decided): the predicate looks only at ecosystems claiming the one colliding bare name, but once a path IS promoted, the rewrite still touches every one of that path's index.native entries across ALL of its ecosystems, including an npm Platform manifest whose own different name never entered the predicate but whose stored owner id must still be updated to the new Prefixed id -- at BOTH rewrite location (2) below (index.platform, keyed by the Platform manifest's own name, required for AC-13) AND rewrite location (3) below (index.native, keyed by that same (ecosystem, own-name) pair, required so a dependency edge naming the Platform manifest by its own name still resolves to the correct, post-promotion owner). Data-structures-and-lifecycle item 3's `path_native_keys` addition (Round-7) is what makes location (3)'s rewrite of this differently-named entry possible for the first-seen path in a branch (i) collision, since `claiming_ecosystems` alone (name-scoped) does not retain it.

LOCAL PROMOTION BOOKKEEPING (see Data-structures-and-lifecycle item 4, ROUND-2 RETYPED): at each collision point where the PROMOTION PREDICATE selects promotion, after computing both paths' newly-promoted PackageId::Prefixed ids AND their respective name-scoped claiming-ecosystem sets (the same sets the predicate just computed), push both (PackageId, claiming-ecosystem-set) pairs -- both sets read from `claiming_ecosystems` (item 3), never recomputed ad hoc -- onto `promoted_siblings.entry(name.clone()).or_default()` -- never push the PackageId alone, since a Case D member's ecosystem set cannot be recovered from its PackageId once stored (a PackageId::Prefixed carries only its single primary_ecosystem field).

ALREADY-PROMOTED-NAME DETECTION (required for AC-07's N>2 case): package_manifest_decls.insert returning Some is not by itself a sufficient trigger, because promotion re-keys both of the first two colliding paths' entries from Bare(name) to their respective Prefixed keys and removes the Bare(name) key entirely (rewrite location (4)). A THIRD (or later) path independently computing primary_id = Bare(name) then inserts under a now-vacant key, its insert returns None, and no collision fires -- it would silently register as Bare(name) instead of joining the promotion group. FIX (ROUND-7 CORRECTION -- single, consistent placement, replacing three previously inconsistent descriptions of when this lookup runs): immediately after primary_id is computed for each path (walk.rs:78), BEFORE any of that path's own writes -- before walk.rs:80-82's index.bare insertion, before the decls loop (walk.rs:84-124), and before package_manifest_decls.insert (walk.rs:126-128) -- look up primary_id.name() in the local promoted_siblings map: (i) if no entry exists yet, this lookup has no effect on this path's iteration; proceed exactly as before this spec's changes through walk.rs:80-82, the decls loop, and package_manifest_decls.insert, i.e. the existing single-collision insert-and-check-Some logic unchanged (branch (i) is detected later, only when that insert returns Some -- not by this lookup); (ii) if an entry already exists (one or more earlier paths already promoted under it), evaluate the disjointness predicate for THIS path's own claiming-ecosystem set (read from `claiming_ecosystems.get(&rel_path)`, item 3 -- ROUND-4: never recomputed ad hoc) against EVERY existing member's RETAINED claiming-ecosystem set stored in that promoted_siblings entry (ROUND-2 CORRECTION: read each stored member's own `BTreeSet<Ecosystem>` directly from the tuple -- do not attempt to re-derive a stored member's claiming-ecosystem set from its bare PackageId alone, since a Case D member's PackageId::Prefixed encodes only its single primary_ecosystem and cannot reconstruct a multi-ecosystem set) -- promote into the group if disjoint from all members -- at this lookup point, promoting means exactly two actions taken immediately, before any of this path's own writes: (a) reassign this path's own `primary_id` local variable in place, from its just-computed pre-promotion Bare value to the newly-promoted PackageId::Prefixed{primary_ecosystem, name} value (per the ORDERING STATEMENT in the GUARD section below, this reassignment must happen before the decls loop, walk.rs:84-124, begins); and (b) push this path's own new (Prefixed id, claiming-ecosystem-set) pair onto promoted_siblings[name]. ROUND-8 CORRECTION: the upfront lookup does NOT itself insert into package_manifest_decls. package_manifest_decls.insert (walk.rs:126-128) is keyed on `primary_id` and valued on `decls` -- the per-manifest declarations the decls loop (walk.rs:84-124) builds for this path -- and at the moment this lookup runs (before the decls loop has executed for this path), `decls` does not yet exist to insert; a prior version of this paragraph incorrectly described the upfront lookup as performing that insert. The actual package_manifest_decls insertion for branch (ii) still happens later, unchanged in position from the original code, at the normal walk.rs:126-128 site -- see the GUARD/ORDERING STATEMENT section below, which correctly states that by that point in this path's iteration, the insertion naturally uses the now-already-correct Prefixed primary_id together with the now-fully-populated decls from the decls loop that ran in between, making it a normal first-time insert under the Prefixed key, not a rewrite and not a special action taken at the lookup point; return DuplicatePackage{id, paths} naming this path and the specific offending existing member's path if not disjoint from any member. This mechanism must be order-independent: by_path is a BTreeMap<PathBuf,..>, so the by-path loop (walk.rs:72) iterates lexicographically by path, not by ecosystem or discovery order, and whichever path is visited second promotes via branch (i) while any later path visits branch (ii).

GUARD AGAINST STALE index.bare RE-INSERTION, SPLIT BY BRANCH (the two strategies below are not interchangeable options -- each branch is implementable only one way): in the CURRENT, unmodified source (pre-implementation), walk.rs:80-82's `index.bare.insert(primary_id.name().to_string(), primary_id.clone())` runs unconditionally at the top of every path iteration -- there is no ALREADY-PROMOTED-NAME DETECTION lookup at all yet, since that lookup is new logic this spec introduces. ROUND-7 CORRECTION (single consistent placement, matching the ALREADY-PROMOTED-NAME DETECTION entry above): this spec's implementation must insert that lookup BEFORE walk.rs:80-82, not after -- i.e. the lookup is the very first thing to run once primary_id is computed (walk.rs:78), ahead of the pre-existing index.bare.insert.

BRANCH (i) (the first pairwise collision, detected only when package_manifest_decls.insert returns Some): by the moment this collision is detected, BOTH colliding paths' index.bare entries have already been unconditionally written -- the first-seen path's, in its own earlier iteration, which has already fully completed; the second, colliding path's, earlier in its own current iteration, at walk.rs:80-82, before the insert-and-check-Some logic that detects the collision even runs. Skip-on-insertion is therefore NOT implementable for branch (i): there is no point before either write where the collision is yet known. BRANCH (i) MUST use remove-at-promotion-time: the instant the PROMOTION PREDICATE selects promotion over DuplicatePackage, both colliding paths' now-stale index.bare entries for that name must be explicitly removed.

BRANCH (ii) (a third-or-later path joining an already-promoted group): by the time a third-or-later path's loop iteration begins, every earlier iteration -- including the one that decided branch (i)'s promotion -- has already fully completed, so the local promoted_siblings map already holds the group's entry before this path's iteration starts. This makes skip-on-insertion possible for branch (ii) specifically: the ALREADY-PROMOTED-NAME DETECTION lookup (checking primary_id.name() against promoted_siblings) MUST be performed, and found, before this path's own walk.rs:80-82 insertion runs. BRANCH (ii) MUST use skip-on-insertion: relocate or gate the walk.rs:80-82 insertion so it never executes at all for a path whose name is already present in promoted_siblings at the top of its own iteration -- never write-then-remove for branch (ii). ORDERING STATEMENT (branch (ii)): when the already-promoted-name lookup for branch (ii) finds an existing promoted_siblings entry and the disjointness check against every existing member passes, this path's own `primary_id` local variable must be reassigned, in place, from its just-computed pre-promotion Bare value to the newly-promoted PackageId::Prefixed{primary_ecosystem, name} value, BEFORE the decls loop (walk.rs:84-124) begins. This means for branch (ii) specifically, index.native (walk.rs:121-123) and index.platform (walk.rs:115-118) are written correctly on their first and only write -- using the already-correct Prefixed primary_id -- and are never stale, never needing the STALE-KEY REWRITE section's locations (2)/(3) applied to them. Only package_manifest_decls (STALE-KEY REWRITE location (4)) still needs an explicit insert-under-the-Prefixed-key action for branch (ii), since that single insertion (walk.rs:126-128) now naturally uses the already-correct Prefixed primary_id -- a normal first-time insert, not a rewrite.

INVARIANT, both branches combined: index.bare must contain no key that has any promoted_siblings entry at the end of build(), for every path ordering and for N=2 as well as N>2 (AC-06 generalized by AC-07 and AC-21).

STALE-KEY REWRITE, FIVE LOCATIONS, ALL REQUIRED: this checklist, as originally written, describes BRANCH (i) exclusively -- the first pairwise collision, where promotion is only known after the decls loop (walk.rs:84-124) has already run with the stale Bare id, genuinely requiring post-hoc correction at all four locations below. BRANCH (ii)'s correct handling (a third-or-later path joining an already-promoted group) is described separately, in the GUARD section's branch (ii) paragraph above, via the primary_id-reassignment-before-the-decls-loop ORDERING STATEMENT -- branch (ii) is handled correctly by never producing a stale write in the first place at locations (1)/(2)/(3), not by applying this checklist's locations (1)/(2)/(3) to it after the fact; only location (4) still applies to branch (ii), as a normal first-time insert rather than a rewrite. When a path's primary_id is promoted to PackageId::Prefixed{primary_ecosystem, name} (primary_ecosystem is the same ecosystem ecosystem_primary_priority, walk.rs:495-501, already selects as that path's primary_id ecosystem -- promotion changes WHAT primary_id is without changing HOW it is selected), all of that path's own index entries populated earlier in the SAME per-path loop iteration must be rewritten from the stale pre-promotion Bare id to the new single Prefixed id: (1) walk.rs:80-82, index.bare -- two different required implementations for the same underlying invariant (index.bare contains no promoted name at the end of build()), not two interchangeable options for the same code path: for BRANCH (i) (both paths' index.bare entries were already unconditionally written, at walk.rs:80-82, before the collision was detected -- see the GUARD section above), the bare-name key must be explicitly removed from index.bare at promotion time -- write-then-remove, not merely left unwritten. For BRANCH (ii) (a third-or-later path joining an already-promoted group), the walk.rs:80-82 insertion must never be written in the first place -- skip-on-insertion, per the GUARD section's branch (ii) rule -- so there is nothing to remove for that path's entry, and "left unwritten" is the correct and required outcome for branch (ii), not a violation to avoid. (2) walk.rs:115-118, index.platform.insert(id.name().to_string(), (primary_id.clone(), manifest_rel, role)) -- the stored owner (primary_id) for this path's own npm Platform manifest (if any) must become the new Prefixed id, or config/groups.rs's index.platform.get(name) lookups (groups.rs:150, :181) resolve a fixed-group/linked-group platform-manifest member to a stale owner id (AC-13). (3) walk.rs:121-123, index.native.insert((*eco, id.name().to_string()), primary_id.clone()) -- ROUND-7 CORRECTION (exact, unambiguous procedure, replacing the prior ambiguous "one per its own ecosystem" phrasing): for BRANCH (i), rewrite index.native by iterating, for BOTH colliding paths, every (Ecosystem, String) pair in that path's own COMPLETE, UNFILTERED key set -- for the current path, its own already-in-scope `list` local (still available in this iteration); for the first-seen path, `path_native_keys.get(&existing_path)` (Data-structures-and-lifecycle item 3's Round-7 addition) -- and for every pair, `index.native.insert((eco, name), <that path's own newly-promoted Prefixed id>)`. This deliberately covers MORE than the name-scoped `claiming_ecosystems` set: `claiming_ecosystems.get(&path)` alone is sufficient only for entries whose native-name equals the colliding bare name itself (where ecosystem and name correspond 1:1 within the promoted group, by construction of the IdentityIndex.prefixed restriction) -- it is NOT sufficient for a path that also has a differently-named manifest sharing it, such as an npm Platform manifest (AC-13's fixture: the promoted Cargo path's own `list` also includes an Npm entry keyed by the Platform manifest's own distinct name, e.g. "@myorg/native-core-linux-x64-gnu", which `claiming_ecosystems` excludes by design but which still received a stale `primary_id`-valued index.native entry at walk.rs:121-123 during that path's original iteration and must still be rewritten here). When the path itself spans two or more ecosystems, every one of its rewritten entries points at the SAME single new Prefixed id, never a distinct Prefixed id per ecosystem -- promotion changes WHAT primary_id is for that path, not HOW MANY distinct promoted identities it has. (4) package_manifest_decls itself (declared walk.rs:53-54, populated walk.rs:126-128) -- keyed on the pre-promotion Bare primary_id, must be re-keyed: the entry already inserted for the first-seen path is removed and reinserted under its newly-promoted Prefixed key, sourced from `existing_decls` (the value now bound by the ROUND-2-corrected `if let Some((existing_path, existing_decls)) = ...` pattern described above -- NOT re-derived or re-read from anywhere else), and the current path's entry is inserted under its own Prefixed key using the current path's own already-in-scope `decls` local variable, rather than causing the DuplicatePackage branch to fire. Neither path's decls are ever substituted for the other's: an implementation that sources both promoted entries from the same decls value fails AC-04/AC-07/AC-09's `.manifests` assertions even if it satisfies every other criterion in this spec. (5) index.prefixed (ROUND-9 ADDITION -- this is a new write this spec introduces, not a pre-existing one: it must be added inside the same decls loop, walk.rs:84-124, alongside index.native's write at walk.rs:121-123, guarded by the IdentityIndex.prefixed api_surface entry's restriction that an entry is only inserted when id.name() == primary_id.name() for that path) -- for BRANCH (i), rewrite index.prefixed by iterating, for BOTH colliding paths, every ecosystem in that path's own NAME-SCOPED claiming-ecosystem set, read from `claiming_ecosystems.get(&existing_path)` (first-seen path) and `claiming_ecosystems.get(&rel_path)` (current path): `claiming_ecosystems` (item 3) is the correct and sufficient source for this location, unlike location (3)'s index.native rewrite, because index.prefixed's own restricted population rule means it never held a differently-named Platform-manifest entry to omit in the first place -- `path_native_keys` is not needed here. For each ecosystem `eco` in that set, `index.prefixed.insert((eco, name.clone()), <that path's own newly-promoted Prefixed id>)`, replacing the stale pre-promotion Bare id. Concretely, for the AC-04 fixture, the two paths' single-member claiming-ecosystem sets ({Cargo} and {Npm}) each rewrite exactly one index.prefixed entry -- (Cargo, "native-core") to Prefixed{Cargo, "native-core"} and (Npm, "native-core") to Prefixed{Npm, "native-core"} -- so the two entries carry two genuinely distinct PackageIds. This matters beyond index.prefixed's own correctness: ResolvedConfig.promoted_siblings' derivation in Workspace::load (Data-structures item 5) groups index.prefixed's entries by name and retains only names whose distinct-id count is 2 or more; an implementation that skips this location leaves both entries at their stale Bare("native-core") value, so that derivation finds a distinct-id count of exactly 1 for "native-core" and drops the name from promoted_siblings entirely, making AC-23 (the only criterion exercising the aggregate.rs:211 ambiguity branch) unsatisfiable. For BRANCH (ii): per the GUARD section's branch (ii) ORDERING STATEMENT, this path's own `primary_id` local is already reassigned to its Prefixed value before the decls loop begins, so this new index.prefixed write -- like index.native and index.platform -- is correct on its first and only write and never needs location (5)'s rewrite applied to it. Confirmed explicitly here because, unlike locations (1)-(4), this write does not exist at all in the pre-implementation source for either branch to be traced against; the same before-the-decls-loop primary_id reassignment that already makes index.native/index.platform correct for branch (ii) applies identically to this new write, since all three are populated from the same in-scope, already-correct `primary_id` local at the same point in the same loop iteration.

An implementation that rewrites only (1) and (3) produces a packages map where the promoted package still carries a stale Bare id in package_manifest_decls, failing AC-04's exact-id assertions. An implementation that fixes (1), (3), (4) but not (2) satisfies AC-04/AC-05/AC-06 but fails AC-13. An implementation that fixes (1)-(4) but not (5) satisfies AC-04 through AC-21 but fails AC-23, since ResolvedConfig.promoted_siblings is derived entirely from index.prefixed and a stale Bare-keyed pair collapses to a distinct-id count of 1, dropping the name from promoted_siblings entirely. An implementation using set-inequality instead of set-disjointness for the PROMOTION PREDICATE incorrectly promotes AC-08's fixture (a Case D {Cargo,Npm} path colliding with a single-ecosystem {Npm} path), minting two Prefixed ids for what must instead be DuplicatePackage, and silently overwriting one path's (Npm, name) index.native entry with the other's -- the exact silent coalescing AC-05 forbids.

COMMENT ACCURACY (implementer guidance for AC-22, not itself a separate testable assertion -- AC-22 covers only the mechanical presence/absence check): the false claim "`id` itself is always PackageId::Bare here" currently appears at TWO locations in walk.rs, both of which must be corrected: (a) walk.rs:160-164, the comment immediately preceding the `package_ecosystems` computation ("The real ecosystem(s) this package's manifests were discovered in. `id` itself is always PackageId::Bare here (see the SPEC-002 AC-5 note below), so this is the only place an ecosystem-prefixed [[package-set]] pattern has anything to match against."); and (b) walk.rs:284-288, the comment block immediately preceding the SPEC-002 AC-5 cross-ecosystem diagnostic loop ("Packages-map keys are ALWAYS PackageId::Bare ... Calling key.ecosystem() would always return None and the diagnostic would never fire -- do NOT use key.ecosystem()."). Both must be corrected to no longer claim packages-map keys or `id` are always PackageId::Bare, since this spec's promotion mechanism produces packages-map entries keyed by PackageId::Prefixed whenever promotion occurs (AC-04 through AC-09, AC-21). The corrected comment at walk.rs:284-288 should still explain why the downstream SPEC-002 AC-5 diagnostic loop (`for (pattern, _) in &cfg.packages` beginning at walk.rs:296) remains correct regardless of whether packages-map keys are Bare or Prefixed: that loop never calls `key.ecosystem()` at all -- it sources every ecosystem value from `pkg.canonical_manifests()`'s own manifest declarations (walk.rs:300-306), never from the map key -- and `pattern.matches(key)` (pattern is always unprefixed here, since prefixed rules `continue` earlier in the same loop, walk.rs:297-298) matches by name alone per `PackageId::matches`'s `(None, _) | (_, None) => true` arm (crates/callisto-model/src/identity.rs:154), independent of whether `key` itself is Bare or Prefixed. This explanatory requirement is implementer guidance for writing a correct, non-misleading comment; it is not an externally observable proposition and is therefore not part of AC-22's own testable assertion (see AC-22). No behavior change is required in either diagnostic loop; only the two comments' now-inaccurate text is corrected.

api_surface.name: IdentityIndex::resolve_native
api_surface.signature: pub fn resolve_native(&self, eco: Ecosystem, name: &str) -> Option<&PackageId>
api_surface.description: Unchanged signature and unchanged same-ecosystem-first, cross-ecosystem-fallback-on-exactly-one-candidate behavior (identity.rs:314-338). Grep of the current codebase (crates/callisto-graph/src and crates/callisto-graph/tests) confirms resolve_native has no production call site anywhere in src/ -- its only callers are three direct unit-test invocations in crates/callisto-graph/tests/ecosystem_bugs_test.rs (lines 267, 274, 309). It is left unchanged not because any real caller class currently depends on its cross-ecosystem fallback -- no such production caller (e.g. a 'group-member resolution' consumer) actually exists in the current codebase -- but because it is a lower-level, general-purpose permissive lookup kept on IdentityIndex's public API surface for forward compatibility: no call site currently needs its behavior changed, and this spec does not remove or narrow public API it has no functional reason to touch. Not the function edge-extraction uses -- see resolve_native_with_fallback below, which edge-extraction (walk.rs:360-364) exclusively calls.

api_surface.name: IdentityIndex::resolve_native_with_fallback
api_surface.signature: pub fn resolve_native_with_fallback<'a>(&'a self, eco: Ecosystem, name: &str, diagnostics: &mut Vec<callisto_model::Diagnostic>) -> Option<&'a PackageId>
api_surface.description: Currently (identity.rs:343-392): fast-path exact-ecosystem match; on miss, collects cross-ecosystem candidates and returns Some for exactly 1 (silently, no diagnostic), None with a diagnostic for 2+, None for 0. This spec's fix: the exactly-1-candidate arm must stop returning Some -- when the same-ecosystem lookup misses, the function returns None regardless of cross-ecosystem candidate count (0, 1, or 2+), matching the intent stated in docs/01-spec.md at lines 6075-6076 ('scoping to the declaring ecosystem is what prevents a Cargo `serde` dependency from resolving to an npm workspace member called `serde`'). That doc passage states the intent for a Cargo-consumer/npm-member direction; this fix applies the same no-cross-ecosystem-fallback rule symmetrically regardless of which ecosystem is the consumer and which is the colliding member (ROUND-9 CORRECTION: this entry previously cited AC-10 here, which is actually the unrelated same-ecosystem crates/dup-a-vs-crates/dup-b DuplicatePackage criterion; the criterion that actually fixtures the reverse, npm-consumer/Cargo-member direction is AC-14 -- an npm consumer depending on a Cargo package named serde, the mirror image of the docs/01-spec.md:6075-6076 Cargo-consumer/npm-member passage cited above). When exactly one cross-ecosystem candidate exists, a Diagnostic (severity Warning, code UnknownPackage) is still pushed naming the ambiguity and suggesting the ecosystem-prefixed spelling (reusing the message-construction logic already present at identity.rs:370-388), and the function returns None in that case too -- this diagnostic-plus-None pairing at the former 1-candidate arm is new behavior at that arm, replacing the prior Some(id)-with-no-diagnostic return. This function's own edge-extraction call site is walk.rs:360-364, inside ManifestWalkResolver::build's dependency-edge loop -- no other call site of this function exists in the current codebase to update.

api_surface.name: ResolvedConfig.promoted_siblings
api_surface.description: ROUND-2 RETYPE (was `BTreeMap<String, Vec<PackageId>>`): a bare PackageId cannot represent a Case D member's full multi-ecosystem claiming set once it is promoted and stored, since PackageId::Prefixed itself encodes only one ecosystem. See Data-structures-and-lifecycle item 5 for the complete population, scope, and timing contract, including exactly how each PackageId's full ecosystem set is reconstructed from IdentityIndex.prefixed's single-ecosystem-keyed entries. New field on ResolvedConfig (crates/callisto-graph/src/config/resolve.rs, struct at resolve.rs:15-42), added parallel to the existing raw_groups/groups deferred-resolution split (resolve.rs:36-40's doc comment: 'kept so that Workspace::load can call GroupTable::resolve once the IdentityIndex is available after ManifestWalkResolver::build'). This is a read-only derivation from IdentityIndex.prefixed (which this spec's AC-02 already requires ManifestWalkResolver::build to populate) -- no new field or accessor is added to ManifestWalkResolver or IdentityIndex to support it.

api_surface.name: resolve_package_config (ambiguity-detecting Result return)
api_surface.signature: pub(crate) fn resolve_package_config<'a>(id: &PackageId, cfg: &'a ResolvedConfig) -> Result<Option<&'a PackageConfig>, GraphError>
api_surface.description:
Current signature (config/resolve.rs:195-198, body at 199-203): `pub(crate) fn resolve_package_config<'a>(id: &PackageId, cfg: &'a ResolvedConfig) -> Option<&'a PackageConfig>`, implemented as a Pass-1 Prefixed-tier `.find()` (resolve.rs:201) `.or_else()`-chained to a Pass-2 Bare-tier `.find()` (resolve.rs:202), then `.map(|(_, pcfg)| pcfg)` (resolve.rs:203) which discards which pass produced the match. This spec changes the return type to `Result<Option<&'a PackageConfig>, GraphError>` and adds no new parameter. Inside Pass 2 (the Bare-tier `.or_else(...)` branch) only -- Pass 1's Prefixed-tier match is never ambiguous (a Prefixed rule_id can match at most one promoted or unpromoted package per ecosystem) and is unaffected -- before returning `Ok(Some(pcfg))`, look up `id.name()` in `cfg.promoted_siblings` (Data-structures-and-lifecycle item 5 or item 6's overlay, depending on which call site); if the entry exists (only ever stored with 2+ pairs), return `Err(GraphError::AmbiguousName { name: id.name().to_string(), candidates })` instead, where `candidates` is built by projecting ONLY the PackageId half out of each stored `(PackageId, BTreeSet<Ecosystem>)` pair -- e.g. `cfg.promoted_siblings[id.name()].iter().map(|(pid, _)| pid.clone()).collect()` -- and dropping the ecosystem-set half entirely, since `GraphError::AmbiguousName`'s `candidates` field (verified against crates/callisto-graph/src/error.rs:87-90 this session) is `Vec<PackageId>`, not a vector of pairs. Pass 1's Ok(Some(pcfg)) path and the final Ok(None) path (neither pass matched) are wrapped in Ok unchanged.

NEW METHOD: `ResolvedConfig::with_promoted_siblings` -- see Data-structures-and-lifecycle item 6 for its exact construction and lifetime.

TWO CALL SITES, per Data-structures-and-lifecycle item 7: (a) walk.rs:175 changes from `let pkg_override = resolve_package_config(&id, cfg);` to `let pkg_override = resolve_package_config(&id, &cfg_with_local_promotions)?;`, where `cfg_with_local_promotions` is constructed once (before the loop starting at walk.rs:144 begins) via `cfg.with_promoted_siblings(promoted_siblings)` -- `cfg` here is build's own `&ResolvedConfig` parameter, `promoted_siblings` is build's own local map (Data-structures item 4, pair-typed), NOT `cfg.promoted_siblings`. (b) aggregate.rs:211-213 changes from `let policy = resolve_package_config(&pkg.id, config)` / `.and_then(|pcfg| pcfg.pre_major_inference)` / `.unwrap_or(PreMajorInferencePolicy::Off);` to the same three lines with a `?` inserted immediately after the `resolve_package_config(&pkg.id, config)` call on line 211 -- `config` here is `aggregate()`'s own received parameter, passed through unmodified, since by the time `aggregate()` runs (via commands/version.rs:39, always after Workspace::load has completed for that config) `config.promoted_siblings` (item 5) is already correctly populated. `with_promoted_siblings` is never called on this path. In both cases resolve_package_config's own signature is unaffected -- still exactly `(id: &PackageId, cfg: &ResolvedConfig) -> Result<Option<&PackageConfig>, GraphError>` -- only which ResolvedConfig reference each call site passes differs. `aggregate()`'s own public signature (aggregate.rs:164-176, including its `where D: DependencyResolver, I: SeverityInference` clause) is unchanged; its one external caller, commands/version.rs:39, requires no change.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given a real discovered Cargo package named foo (project root path 'crates/foo', ecosystem Cargo, the only package anywhere in the workspace declaring the bare name "foo" in any ecosystem, so this fixture triggers no promotion) and a callisto.toml with `[[fixed-group]]\nname = "g"\nmembers = ["cargo:foo"]`, loading the workspace via Workspace::load succeeds and the resolved fixed group's members contain GroupMember::Package(PackageId::Bare("foo".to_string())) -- the package's own concrete, unpromoted identity, matching the fixture's single Cargo package -- and no GraphError::MissingGroupMember is raised for that member.

For the workspace in AC-01, after Workspace::load succeeds, IdentityIndex.prefixed contains an entry keyed (Ecosystem::Cargo, "foo".to_string()) whose value equals the PackageId that IdentityIndex.native.get(&(Ecosystem::Cargo, "foo".to_string())) also returns for that same package -- the same identity is reachable through both the native map and the prefixed map for every discovered (ecosystem, native-name) pair whose manifest declares the same name as its own path's primary identity (i.e. every pair IdentityIndex.prefixed actually contains, per the restricted population rule stated in the IdentityIndex.prefixed api_surface entry). This does not extend to a differently-named manifest sharing that path, such as an npm platform manifest: that manifest's own distinct name never gains a prefixed entry, by design (see IdentityIndex.prefixed and AC-13). Checked as a direct map lookup (not only indirectly via AC-01's group resolution succeeding).

Given the same workspace as AC-01 but with members = ["npm:foo"] where no npm package named foo exists anywhere in the workspace (only the Cargo package foo exists), loading the workspace via Workspace::load returns Err(GraphError::MissingGroupMember { group, member }) with member == "npm:foo" -- an ecosystem-prefixed spelling for an ecosystem in which the name does not exist must still fail, not silently match the wrong ecosystem's foo.

Given a Cargo crate at crates/native-core (Cargo.toml package.name = "native-core") and an unrelated npm package at packages/native-core (package.json name = "native-core"), with no shared directory and no callisto.toml config referencing either by ecosystem-prefixed spelling, building the workspace via ManifestWalkResolver::build succeeds (Ok, not Err(GraphError::DuplicatePackage)), and the resulting packages map contains exactly two entries: one with id == PackageId::Prefixed { ecosystem: Ecosystem::Cargo, name: "native-core".to_string() } and one with id == PackageId::Prefixed { ecosystem: Ecosystem::Npm, name: "native-core".to_string() }. Additionally, the Cargo-id entry's `.manifests` field contains exactly one ManifestDecl, whose `path` is crates/native-core/Cargo.toml, and the Npm-id entry's `.manifests` field contains exactly one ManifestDecl, whose `path` is packages/native-core/package.json -- neither entry's `.manifests` contains a ManifestDecl belonging to the other path; an implementation that sources both promoted packages' decls from the same underlying Vec (e.g. by discarding and never rebinding the first-seen path's own decls at the package_manifest_decls collision point) would satisfy the id-count assertion above while still failing this manifests assertion.

For the workspace in AC-04, IdentityIndex.native contains both (Ecosystem::Cargo, "native-core") mapping to the Cargo package's PackageId and (Ecosystem::Npm, "native-core") mapping to the distinct Npm package's PackageId -- the two identities are never coalesced into one entry, and neither entry retains the pre-promotion Bare id.

For the workspace in AC-04, IdentityIndex.bare does not contain any key "native-core" -- once both occurrences are promoted to PackageId::Prefixed, the bare spelling becomes genuinely ambiguous and must not resolve through the bare map at all. A config or dependency reference using the unprefixed spelling "native-core" resolves via IdentityIndex::resolve_human (identity.rs:252-298): with two Prefixed candidates collected into `candidates` (identity.rs:267-272), the candidates.is_empty() check at identity.rs:288 is false, so neither the single-candidate return (identity.rs:274-276, requires candidates.len() == 1) nor the sibling-disambiguation return (identity.rs:278-286, requires a non-empty siblings slice, never supplied by either of resolve_human's call sites in config/groups.rs) fires; execution reaches the final else branch (identity.rs:292-297), returning Err(GraphError::AmbiguousName{name: "native-core".to_string(), candidates}) rather than silently picking one of the two Prefixed identities.

Given three packages sharing the bare name "multi" across three distinct ecosystems at three different paths -- a Cargo crate, an Npm package, and a Pypi package, each named "multi" -- building the workspace via ManifestWalkResolver::build succeeds (Ok, not Err(GraphError::DuplicatePackage)) and the resulting packages map contains exactly three entries: id == PackageId::Prefixed{Cargo, "multi"}, id == PackageId::Prefixed{Npm, "multi"}, and id == PackageId::Prefixed{Pypi, "multi"}, one per ecosystem, for every possible by-path iteration order (by_path is a BTreeMap<PathBuf,..>, so the real iteration order is lexicographic by path, not by ecosystem or discovery order). Each of the three entries' `.manifests` field contains exactly the one ManifestDecl belonging to that entry's own original path (e.g. the Prefixed{Cargo, "multi"} entry's `.manifests` contains only the Cargo crate's own manifest, never a manifest from the Npm or Pypi path) -- no entry's `.manifests` contains a decl bled over from any of the other two paths. This criterion depends on, and is satisfied only by, the ALREADY-PROMOTED-NAME DETECTION mechanism described in the ManifestWalkResolver::build api_surface entry -- the second and later paths to claim "multi" must be checked against the local promoted_siblings group already recorded for that name, checked against every existing group member, not merely against a single prior package_manifest_decls entry, or the third path's collision goes undetected and it registers as Bare("multi") instead of promoting.

Given a genuine Case D package at crates/foo (Cargo.toml package.name = "foo" and package.json name = "foo", both manifests at the same path, so this path's name-scoped claiming-ecosystem set for the bare name "foo" is {Cargo, Npm}) and a second, unrelated npm-only package at packages/foo (package.json name = "foo", no Cargo.toml anywhere at that path, claiming-ecosystem set {Npm}), building the workspace via ManifestWalkResolver::build returns Err(GraphError::DuplicatePackage { id, paths }) where id == PackageId::Bare("foo".to_string()) and paths contains both "crates/foo" and "packages/foo" in some order -- not a promotion, and not Ok(_) -- because the two paths' claiming-ecosystem sets ({Cargo, Npm} and {Npm}) share Npm and are therefore not disjoint, even though they also differ (the sets are unequal). This is the case a set-inequality promotion predicate gets wrong and a set-disjointness predicate gets right: a Case D package's already-established dual identity (one Package, one primary_id spanning both Cargo and Npm) must never be silently discarded by treating a partial ecosystem overlap as grounds for cross-ecosystem promotion. This criterion is observable only through build()'s returned Err value (its id and paths fields): build() returns Err on this path before ever constructing or returning a Self/IdentityIndex, so no IdentityIndex field (index.native, index.bare, or otherwise) is ever exposed in a returned value for this scenario, and no assertion is made, or can be made, about internal map state.

Given the standard maturin/PyO3 layout -- a Rust crate at bindings/rust (Cargo.toml package.name = "mylib") and its Python binding at bindings/python (pyproject.toml project.name = "mylib"), sibling directories, no shared path -- building the workspace succeeds without GraphError::DuplicatePackage, producing two distinct packages with id == PackageId::Prefixed{Cargo, "mylib"} and id == PackageId::Prefixed{Pypi, "mylib"} respectively. The Cargo-id entry's `.manifests` field contains exactly one ManifestDecl whose path is bindings/rust/Cargo.toml, and the Pypi-id entry's `.manifests` field contains exactly one ManifestDecl whose path is bindings/python/pyproject.toml -- neither entry's `.manifests` contains the other path's decl. (Distinct fixture from AC-04 and AC-07: a two-ecosystem, non-Npm pairing, verifying the promotion predicate is not accidentally Npm-specific.)

Given a Cargo crate at crates/dup-a (name = "dup") and a second, unrelated Cargo crate at crates/dup-b (name = "dup") -- same ecosystem, two different paths -- building the workspace returns Err(GraphError::DuplicatePackage { id, paths }) where paths contains both "crates/dup-a" and "crates/dup-b" in some order, matching the pre-existing, unchanged same-ecosystem collision behavior (both paths' claiming-ecosystem sets are the singleton {Cargo}, which is not disjoint from itself).

Given a genuine Case D package at one directory (Cargo.toml name = "foo", package.json name = "@myorg/foo", both at path 'crates/foo', neither name "foo" nor "@myorg/foo" claimed by any other package anywhere in the workspace), building the workspace succeeds and produces exactly one Package with id == PackageId::Bare("foo".to_string()) (unchanged from current behavior: the same-path collapse via ecosystem_primary_priority happens before the cross-path collision check, and this path never collides with any other path, so no promotion is triggered).

Given a Cargo package foo at crates/foo and no npm package named foo anywhere in the workspace, and a separate npm package consumer at packages/consumer whose package.json declares "dependencies": {"foo": "^1.0.0"}, building the workspace's dependency edges does not resolve consumer's "foo" dependency to the Cargo package foo's PackageId -- ws.graph.edges() contains no DepEdge with to == the Cargo foo's PackageId and from == consumer's PackageId; the dependency is treated as unresolved/external and produces no edge for that entry. Separately, ws.graph.diagnostics() contains a Diagnostic with code == DiagnosticCode::UnknownPackage, severity == DiagnosticSeverity::Warning, and message containing the string "foo" and the word "ambiguous" or "cargo:foo" -- the miss is surfaced, not silent, even though no edge is created.

Given a Cargo crate at crates/native-core (Cargo.toml package.name = "native-core") that also has an npm platform manifest at its own directory (crates/native-core/package.json, os/cpu-constrained, name = "@myorg/native-core-linux-x64-gnu", detected via detect_npm_role as ManifestRole::Platform, whose declared name is distinct from "native-core" so this path's claiming-ecosystem set for "native-core" stays {Cargo}), and an unrelated npm package at packages/native-core (package.json name = "native-core", claiming-ecosystem set {Npm}) promoted alongside it per AC-04 (so the Cargo crate's primary_id is promoted from Bare("native-core") to Prefixed{Cargo, "native-core"}, {Cargo} disjoint from {Npm}), plus a callisto.toml with `[[fixed-group]]\nname = "g"\nmembers = ["@myorg/native-core-linux-x64-gnu"]`, loading the workspace via Workspace::load succeeds and the resolved fixed group's members contain a GroupMember::PlatformManifest whose owner field equals PackageId::Prefixed{Cargo, "native-core"} -- not the stale, pre-promotion PackageId::Bare("native-core"). Verified end-to-end through GroupTable::resolve's index.platform.get(name) lookup (config/groups.rs:150), confirming IdentityIndex.platform's stored owner for the platform manifest's own name (walk.rs:115-118) was rewritten at promotion time, not left stale.
